text.p: Elizabeth Noyce, the former wife of microchip co-inventor Robert Noyce, who gave away millions of dollars as a philantriphist helping to protect jobs died Wednesday at age 65.
Noyce died in her sleep at her coastal Maine home. The cause of death was not immediately known, but Noyce had suffered from emphysema for several years, spokesman Owen Wells said.
Noyce and her husband divorced in 1975 and she received half of the massive fortune he had built through the microchip invention and the founding of Fairchild Semiconductor and Intel Corp.

Wells said Noyce saw her fortune as tool to protect Maine's economy. Among her recent projects was the purchase of several office buildings in Portland and an effort to revitalise the downtown of the state's largest city.
Noyce had substancial holdings of Intel stock and Wells acknowledged that the stocks' recent increase in price made it difficult to determine her exact worth.
